response.sql:
WITH actor_counts AS (
  SELECT actor_id, COUNT(*) AS film_count
  FROM film_actor
  GROUP BY actor_id
),
totals AS (
  SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT film_id) AS total_films
  FROM film_actor
),
ratios AS (
  SELECT ac.actor_id, ac.film_count, ac.film_count * 1.0 / t.total_films AS ratio
  FROM actor_counts ac
  CROSS JOIN totals t
)
SELECT r.actor_id, r.film_count, r.ratio, r.ratio - (SELECT AVG(ratio) FROM ratios) AS diff_from_avg
FROM ratios r
ORDER BY diff_from_avg DESC
LIMIT 10;

assumptions.assumption: The number of films an actor is credited in is the row count per actor_id in film_actor, which is valid because (actor_id, film_id) is the primary key so each row is a distinct film.
The denominator is COUNT(DISTINCT film_id) over film_actor (the films that have at least one credit), not the full film table.
The average is the unweighted mean of the per-actor ratios over the actors that appear in film_actor, not over every row of the actor table.
Ties in diff_from_avg are left in an arbitrary order because the request does not specify a tie-breaker, so the top 10 cut may split tied rows.
